newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa retraces sharply to end mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa retraces sharply to end mostly lower.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures retraced sharply from session highs to end Thursday mostly lower on stop-loss selling as the market made its way lower.
Traders said New York's reversal from overnight's chart-driven rally dented sentiment in London.
But they said technically the market looked firm and could rebound in the coming days.
"We may have another attempt at the highs," said one.

In one of the most volatile sessions for days, December rose early to clear the psychologically-important 1,000 stg barrier on speculative and trade buying before selling set in to drive the contract to a low of 986 stg.
The second position ended at 989 stg a tonne, down four from Wednesday's finish, after rising to a high of 1,002, the highest level seen since September 16.
Traders noted some stop-loss selling at 990 and 986 stg.
Traders had said that further rallies in New York would help firmly push December above the stiff 1,000-level resistance. But follow-through buying failed to materialise.
The September/December spread narrowed to 11 stg from 29 stg the previous day.
Volume was a modest 4,896 lots, up from Wednesday's 3,036.
Cocoa had been capped within a tight 980-990 band for the past days on lack of origin news and flimsy grinder interest partly stemming from sterling's strength against most European currencies.
Traders said Wednesday's news that Ivory Coast would open its 1996/97 cocoa marketing year on October 15 could have boosted sentiment.
Traditionally, the market tends to rally ahead of the opening of the season.
